# v3.31.0

Covers everything since **v3.30.0**.

This release is about **consistency across the pages you actually use**. The dashboard, the 12 reports, the program and offering dashboards, and the student and training pages had each been built at different times, and had quietly drifted apart — filters in one place on one report and somewhere else on the next, export buttons in three different corners, four different geography pickers that behaved differently from one another.

Nothing about your data changes, and no report produces a different number than it did before. What changes is where the controls are and how they behave, so that knowing one page now means knowing all of them.

## Changed — every report has the same shape

All 12 reports now follow one layout, top to bottom:

**Page heading** (with a named "back" link and the export button in the top right) → **filters** → **the headline numbers** → **charts** → **the results table**.

The filters moved. Previously seven reports kept them inside the results table's own box, three floated them in a bare row, and one hid them in a chart's header. That was actively misleading: on every report the filters drive **the headline numbers and the charts as well as the table**, and tucking them inside the table implied they only narrowed the rows underneath. They now sit in their own card directly under the page heading, where their scope is obvious.

Within that card the controls are always in the same order — search, then geography, then the report's own dropdowns, then dates, then grouping, then tick-boxes — and the export button is now in the top right of the page heading on every report, instead of moving around.

## Changed — the geography filter works the same way everywhere

Every page that filters by location now uses one **cascading** picker: choosing a theatre narrows the list of regions, choosing a region narrows the list of countries, and changing a higher level clears the ones below it.

There used to be four different versions of this control, and three of them did not cascade. One difference is worth knowing about because it changes what you see:

- **A country with no completions is now offered in the list.** The older filters built their options from the data that happened to be present, so a country with nothing recorded against it was silently absent — indistinguishable from one you had never set up. Selecting it now returns an honest empty result, which tells you the country exists and has no data, rather than leaving you to wonder whether you mis-remembered the name.

The cascading filter is now on all 12 reports, the dashboard and the training catalogue.

## Changed — help that matches the page you are on

Every report now has **its own help entry**. Eight of them previously shared one generic "reports" page, which could describe the filters of a report you were not looking at. One help link that led nowhere has also been fixed.

## Fixed

- **A fifth metric card no longer strands on its own row.** Three reports show five headline figures, and the strip was fixed at four across, so the fifth wrapped onto an otherwise empty line.
- **The export menu on the program compliance pages now closes when you click away from it.** It previously stayed open until you clicked the button a second time.
- **The Comparison and Learner Scorecard reports now show the "N results" count** that every other report displays above its table.
- **The training catalogue no longer leaves a stale region or country in the page address**, so a link copied from it reopens the view you were actually looking at.

## Changed — the student record

- **The count of legacy certifications is an orange badge again**, with the explanation that those certifications are retired and need renewing or replacing. It had briefly become a line of plain grey text; a number you are meant to *notice* is not the same as one you might read.
- **The student's name sits back inside the details card**, rather than floating above it.

## Under the hood

Buttons, dropdowns, search boxes, filter cards and loading indicators are now drawn from one shared set rather than being written out separately on each page, so they no longer drift apart as pages are added. An unused internal endpoint left over from an earlier version has been removed.

## For administrators

Nothing to do, and nothing to plan for. There is no database change, no configuration change, and no change to any number the system reports. Update as you normally would.
